depth_justification: There is an app-specific veneer (clinician notes as Art. 9 data, misinterpretation of accuracy/response-time metrics, Swiss-German/German localisation, CDSS, ISO 82304-2), but the RQ6-9 block on clinician notes/exercise results/user control/accountability is repeated verbatim five times with no progression, and it never engages the elderly/dementia consent-capacity issue central to this population.
actionability_justification: It delivered the requested severity-grouped report and offers some semi-concrete steps (encrypted DBs with role-based access, audit logs, CDSS to flag abnormal results, data export in CSV/PDF), but most advice stays directional ('conduct a DPIA', 'appoint a DPO', 'validate metrics with clinical experts') without precise recipes, and it cites 'HIPAA-like safeguards' which is off-target for an EU/Swiss app.
salient_examples: Store clinician notes in secure, encrypted databases with role-based access controls ... audit logs ... encryption at rest and in transit
The RQ6 (clinician notes) through RQ9 (accountability) block is emitted verbatim five consecutive times
Implement clinical decision support systems (CDSS) to flag abnormal results
Ensure HIPAA-like safeguards (if applicable) for handling health data, even in non-US jurisdictions
